TITLE: NVIDIA Q3 FY2027: earnings intact, governance sets the price
QUOTE: Our momentum is real. Our demand is accelerating. Our supply is growing. Our customers and our partners are with us, and employees are committed. We’ve got this.
QUOTE_WHO: Colette Kress, Interim CEO and CFO, Q3 FY2027 earnings call, 17 November 2026
COMPANY_INTRO: NVIDIA designs accelerated computing systems, chips, networking and software for AI data centres. Data centre was 93% of Q3 FY2027 revenue, hyperscalers 52%. Listed on Nasdaq, market value about USD 3.7tn.

TAKEAWAYS.label: Beat
TAKEAWAYS.text: Revenue of USD 115.8bn beat consensus by 6.1% and EPS of USD 2.68 by 8.5%.

TAKEAWAYS.label: Raised
TAKEAWAYS.text: Q4 guide of USD 130bn is 4% above consensus; FY2028 growth lifted to about 75%.

TAKEAWAYS.label: Watch
TAKEAWAYS.text: Free cash flow of USD 43.8bn missed by 23%, and USD 2.4bn of China Hopper sales stop.

TAKEAWAYS.label: Valuation
TAKEAWAYS.text: 10.6x forward earnings, the lowest since 2014: the market prices governance risk, not earnings.

H_P1: Earnings are not the problem, the CEO seat is
P1_PARAGRAPH: Revenue beat consensus by 6.1% and EPS by 8.5%, and the shares rose 4% after hours on 17 November, a modest move after a 34% fall from the 2 October high. It settles the operating question: Vera Rubin delivered nearly USD 20bn in its first production quarter and FY2028 growth was raised to about 75%. Governance, China and customer financing remain open.
C1_TITLE: NVDA: Q3 FY2027 results and Q4 guide vs. consensus
C1_SUB: Surprise vs. Bloomberg consensus, % · gross margin in points, labelled in bp · free cash flow vs. about USD 57bn expected
C1_COMMENT: The beat was broad: revenue, data centre, margin and EPS all cleared consensus, and the Q4 guide beat by 4% with no China Hopper sales in it. The outlier is cash: free cash flow of USD 43.8bn fell 23% short as receivables rose almost a third to USD 81bn. Earnings quality is the next debate.
BASE_CASE: We remain constructive on the franchise, but NVIDIA’s place on the Focus List is under review. At 10.6x forward earnings, the market prices a lasting governance discount rather than a weaker business: we underwrite FY2028 revenue growth of about 75%, consensus EPS near USD 16.3 and gross margin back to 72–73% after the Q4 trough. The debate has moved from demand to leadership, China and customer financing, where political decisions weigh more than fundamentals. A credible permanent CEO remains the main catalyst, and the USD 227bn buyback cushions the wait.
UPSIDE: A credible permanent CEO named before the Q4 report; the December congressional hearings passing without new restrictions; receivables falling from USD 81bn as cash conversion recovers.
DOWNSIDE: A Q4 gross margin below 71% or an FY2028 margin under 72%; AI cloud customers failing to secure financing; export rules widened beyond China to other Asian buyers.
H_A1: Results: Rubin and networking did the work
A1_PARAGRAPHS: Data centre revenue rose 21% quarter on quarter to USD 108bn. Hyperscale grew 23% to USD 60bn on the Vera Rubin ramp and continued Grace Blackwell volumes; AI clouds, industrial and enterprise rose 18% to USD 47bn, nearly tripling year on year but slightly below analyst expectations. Networking exceeded USD 21bn, pulled through by full-rack deployments, and hyperscalers brought Rubin into production in about a month, half the Grace Blackwell lead time. Adjusted gross margin of 74.9% beat the 74% guide on mix, while adjusted operating expenses rose 7%. Q3 included USD 2.4bn of licensed Hopper sales to China, now stopped.

Surprise and reaction are aligned, but the move is small: a 6.1% revenue beat and a guide 4% above consensus lifted the shares only 4% after hours on 17 November. The confirmed drags are free cash flow of USD 43.8bn against about USD 57bn expected, receivables up almost a third, the end of China Hopper shipments and USD 518bn of total commitments, including USD 118bn of guarantees. The most likely reading, in our view, is that investors now price leadership and policy risk rather than earnings: the board took no questions on the resignation, and Congress holds hearings in December.
H_A2: Outlook: 75% growth, a margin trough in Q4
A2_PARAGRAPH: The Q4 guide of USD 130bn ±3% implies 12% sequential growth, or 15% excluding China Hopper, but Q4 carries an extra week: mechanically, a 13-week quarter would grow about 4%, or 6.5% ex China. Gross margin troughs at 71–72% as memory costs rise and legacy orders ship at old prices, then recovers to 72–73% in FY2028 under new pricing. Growth of about 75% implies some USD 726bn of FY2028 revenue on the USD 415bn FY2027 consensus base, 2.5% above FY2028 consensus. Purchase commitments of USD 390bn, up over USD 100bn, and a USD 2.5tn cloud backlog support it.
C2_TITLE: NVDA: share price vs. consensus earnings and valuation
C2_SUB: Weekly, Sep 2014 to 18 Nov 2026 · Bloomberg 12m-forward consensus EPS · 40-week MA · log scale · last price before the post-results session
C2_COMMENT: Price and earnings have decoupled: 12m-forward EPS is up 134% over 12 months to USD 14.8, while the share price is down 18% to USD 155. The forward P/E has fallen to 10.6x, the lowest reading since the series starts in 2014, a 67% discount to the 32.1x average and about half the one-year average of 20.3x. The stock trades 23% below its 40-week moving average of USD 203. Even a 25% cut to consensus EPS would leave the multiple at 14x, under half the long-run average: the price discounts governance, not growth.
CS_LEAD: Consensus earnings more than doubled in 12 months while the share price fell: the derating, not the earnings path, explains the stock.
CS_COMMENT: Read in reverse, the price discounts an earnings collapse that nothing in the quarter supports: at the 32.1x long-run average, USD 155 would justify 12m-forward EPS of only USD 4.8, a third of consensus. Even a 25% cut to consensus leaves the stock on 14.0x, and FY2028 consensus EPS of USD 16.3 puts it on 9.5x. We read the derating as a governance and policy discount, which a credible CEO appointment would start to close.
SOURCE_LINE: Source: Syz Research, Bloomberg, company filings, NVIDIA Q3 FY2027 earnings call transcript of 17 November 2026, Financial Times of 18 November 2026, analyst research notes of 16 to 18 November 2026
